topic: x³ at x = −1: secants to tangent
learning_objective: See why the slope of x³ at x = −1 is 3, by watching secant lines turn into the tangent line.

definitions.meaning: a line through two points of a curve
the line that touches the curve at one point with the same steepness as the curve there
f′(x₀) = the limit of (f(x₀ + h) − f(x₀)) / h as h → 0

steps: Here is the curve f(x) = x³.
We want the steepness of the curve exactly at the point P = (−1, −1).
Pick a second point Q, a distance h to the right, and draw the line through P and Q.
The slope of this secant line works out to Slope = 3 − 3h + h².
Now slide Q toward P by shrinking h.
With h = 0.01 the secant slope is already 2.97.
In the limit, the secant lines become the tangent line.
So the derivative at x = −1 is 3: the slope of the tangent line.
examples: With h = 1 the secant slope is 1.
conclusion: f′(−1) = 3; the tangent line at P is y = 3x + 2.
